Article Title: 10 years of UPI: PM Modi hails India’s digital payments milestone and massive reach
Article Text:
PM Modi said the launch of UPI 10 years ago marked a “major turning point” in India’s digital payments journey (Photo: PTI).

NEW DLEHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday marked a decade of the Unified Payments Interface (UPI), describing its scale and reach as a milestone in India’s digital payments journey and calling on citizens to share how the platform has affected their lives.In a post on X, PM Modi said the launch of UPI 10 years ago marked a “major turning point” in India’s digital payments journey."A decade ago, UPI was rolled out, marking a major turning point in India’s digital payments journey. The sheer scale and reach of UPI are something every Indian must be proud of. Tell me about your UPI experience and how it impacted your life..."UPI has become a widely used digital payments platform in India, allowing users to make instant bank-to-bank payments through mobile devices.The 10-year milestone highlights the expansion of digital payments across the country, with UPI becoming an important part of everyday transactions.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi marks a decade of the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) PM Modi calls on citizens to share how the platform has affected their lives. UPI has become a widely used digital payments platform in India, allowing users to make instant bank-to-bank payments through mobile devices.

Article Title: Prevent misuse of data by private entities, SC tells government
Article Text:
SC flags private access to sensitive PF, I-T data, asks Centre to prevent misuse by firms

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Monday expressed concern about a commercial technological ecosystem which allegedly accesses, retrieves and verifies sensitive individual information on provident fund and income tax returns and told the Centre about the desirability of devising an antidote to the problem with the assistance of domain experts.Hearing a PIL by Piyush Sharma, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana noted the matter essentially fell within policy domain but termed private access to sovereign data - individual information given to govt under legislative mandate - and its commercial exploitation as worrisome.Petitioner said his personal inquiry into the issue had revealed that "upon merely furnishing PAN and UAN details to a private verification workflow, the petitioner received complete employment history corresponding the said identifiers. No OTP authentication was generated. No explicit consent was obtained. No visible authorisation-based identity verification process was undertaken".Without blaming govt agencies for any leakage of data, the petitioner highlighted the insecure status of individual data given to govt under the mandate of different laws, as they are accessed at will by private entities."Despite the statutory architecture governing EPFO and I-T data, there appears to be an emerging and concerning pattern wherein private employment verification ecosystems rely upon data corresponding to statutory employment and financial records for purposes such as employment verification, moonlighting detection, dual employment screening, labour market profiling and employment decision-making," he said.SC agreed it was a serious matter but said it must be dealt with through a policy decision. On learning the petitioner sent two comprehensive representations on the issues to Centre, it asked govt to take "necessary steps to prevent misuse of individual data by private enterprises."
Article Summary: SC flags private access to sensitive PF, I-T data, asks Centre to prevent misuse by firms. Petitioner said his personal inquiry into the issue had revealed that "upon merely furnishing PAN and UAN details to a private verification workflow, the petitioner received complete employment history corresponding the said identifiers"

Article Title: 22 million hectares of degraded land restored during 2011 and 2020
Article Text:
India restores nearly 22 million hectares of degraded land, says Bhupender Yadav at UN conference

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India has restored nearly 22 million hectares of degraded and deforested land during the 2011-20 period as against its target of restoring 26 million hectares by 2030, said Union minister Bhupender Yadav at a UN conference Monday.While addressing the 17th session (COP17) of the UNCCD conference in Ulaanbaatar in Mongolia, he also pitched for "diversified, adequate, predictable and sustained international finance" for land restoration and drought resilience, saying it is not a cost, but an investment in food, water, biodiversity, livelihood and long-term resilience.Underlining how the country's restoration efforts had generated approximately 1.2 billion person-days of employment during the 2011-20 period, he said these figures demonstrated restoration could deliver both environmental and socio-economic outcomes by reviving degraded landscapes while creating employment and supporting rural livelihoods.According to India’s second progress report on its land restoration efforts, covering the period 2011–2020, Telangana restored the maximum (4.2 million hectares) degraded area followed by Madhya Pradesh (3.8 million ha), Odisha (2.6 million ha), Gujarat (1.7 million ha) and Andhra Pradesh (1.6 million ha) through afforestation, water resource management, sustainable farming practices, agroforestry, mangrove restoration and natural regeneration of formerly forested land.India’s Desertification and Land Degradation Atlas shows that 97.8 million ha of land, or nearly 29.8% of the country’s geographical area, are affected by land degradation and desertification. Around 82% of India’s degraded land falls in nine states/UT - Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Jammu & Kashmir, Karnataka, Jharkhand, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh and Telangana.Highlighting India’s innovative and diversified financing architecture for land restoration and drought resilience, Yadav noted the ‘Sovereign Green Bonds’ as an avenue to mobilise capital and underlined the country’s ‘Green Credit Programme’, which enables public and private entities to finance restoration of degraded forest land.Though the minister during his address flagged India’s experience demonstrating what the committed domestic resources can achieve, he stressed that this cannot substitute for “additional, adequate and predictable international finance” for restoration and drought resilience.
Article Summary: India has restored nearly 22 million hectares of degraded and deforested land during the 2011-20 period as against its target of restoring 26 million hectares by 2030. Union minister Bhupender Yadav also pitched for "diversified, adequate, predictable and sustained international finance" for land restoration.

Article Title: Amit Shah focuses on new doctrine to fight terror & radicalisation
Article Text:
Amit Shah calls for stronger counter-terror training, faster trials and action against foreign-based masterminds

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah Monday emphasised enhanced training for implementing the country's first-ever counter-terrorism and counter-radicalisation doctrine, Prahaar, and expediting trial in cases with cross-border linkages by bringing back fugitives and using trial in absentia to bring foreign-based masterminds to justice.In his inaugural address at the two-day National Security Strategies Conference, being attended by over 850 officials from the security forces, agencies and police forces, Shah directed that an artificial intelligence-based analysis of information available on multi-agency centre (MAC) platforms be done to create standard operating procedures to counter various security challenges.The Union minister instructed all the agencies to take strict measures against infiltration and asked police forces to adopt a comprehensive and integrated approach while investigating Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act cases.The first day of the conference focused on discussing critical aspects of national security, including response to counter-terrorism challenges; fusion, analysis and operationalisation of intelligence through MAC; vision document on narcotics control; detection and deportation of illegal migrants; a policy framework to combat cyber-crime; and proxy warfare by Pakistan.On Tuesday, the conference will deliberate on the threat landscape from sub-aerial systems and formulating countermeasures, securing the blue economy, information warfare and its implications on national security, and the need for a bio-security framework.Prior to inaugurating the conference, the home minister paid tribute at the martyrs' column here, honouring the supreme sacrifice of Intelligence Bureau personnel to safeguard national security and integrity.The conference, being held in hybrid format, was attended by junior home ministers, deputy NSAs, heads of central paramilitary forces, DGPs of states and UTs, young cops working at the cutting-edge level and experts from specialised fields.

Article Title: SC to consider Tarun Tejpal's plea for exemption from surrender
Article Text:
SC to decide on Tejpal’s plea against surrender after 10-year rape conviction

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Monday said it would pass order on former Tehelka editor Tarun Tejpal 's plea seeking exemption from surrender after Bombay High Court convicted and sentenced him to 10 years of imprisonment in a 2013 rape case, with Goa govt opposing his plea and contending that his appeal was not admissible since the convict had not filed a separate application seeking exemption from surrender or shown a certificate that he has already surrendered as per Order XXII Rule 5 of the Supreme Court Rules, 2013.The matter was heard by a single judge, Justice Alok Aradhe. Solicitor general Tushar Mehta, appearing for the state govt, contended that existence of the appeal was dependent on Tejpal either filing a certificate that he has surrendered or, alternatively, requesting the court to allow an exemption from surrender.Senior advocate Kapil Sibal, representing Tejpal, said there was no need to surrender yet since the high court itself had granted him time to surrender. "This rule doesn't apply because this is a case where stay has been granted by the high court, so there is no question of applying this rule. Suppose the court says no stay, I will have to go to jail," Sibal said, requesting the court to list the appeal for Aug 31.After hearing both sides, Justice Aradhe said he would pass an appropriate order in the matter.The Goa bench of Bombay high court convicted Tejpal under multiple provisions of the IPC and sentenced him to 10 years rigorous imprisonment each under sections 376(2)(f) and 376(2)(k), with the sentences to run concurrently. It also imposed additional concurrent sentences for offences relating to outraging a woman's modesty, sexual harassment, disrobing, wrongful restraint and wrongful confinement. The fines imposed on Tejpal total Rs 10.1 lakh, which the court directed to be paid to the victim. tnn
Article Summary: Supreme Court will pass order on former Tehelka editor Tarun Tejpal's plea seeking exemption from surrender. Bombay High Court convicted and sentenced him to 10 years of imprisonment in a 2013 rape case. Goa govt opposing his plea and contending that his appeal was not admissible.

Article Title: 3 Bambiha members deported from Malaysia
Article Text:
Three Bambiha gang operatives deported from Malaysia in major crackdown, says Amit Shah

NEW DELHI: In a major operation against the Bambiha criminal network, Indian agencies have executed a coordinated crackdown on its key overseas operatives, deporting three of its members from Malaysia who were ordering hits and carrying out extortions in India on behalf of the group's kingpin Lucky Patial.Announced by Union home minister Amit Shah on X Monday, the high-profile action targeted Jaspreet Singh (alias Jas Behbal) of Faridkot, alongside Ajay Singh (alias Ajay Malaysia) and Pawandeep Singh, both from Rajasthan's Sri Ganganagar district. Shah posted that Indian agencies had got the three absconding gangsters apprehended in Malaysia and deported to India."The fugitives....are linked to the Bambiha gang and are accused of multiple crimes, including extortion, cross-border arms and narco-trafficking, and a foiled grenade attack in Ludhiana...our agencies have facilitated the deportation of 51 hardened criminals in 2026 alone."
Article Summary: Three Bambiha operatives deported from Malaysia in major crackdown, says Amit Shah. High-profile action targeted Jaspreet Singh of Faridkot, Ajay Singh of Rajasthan and Pawandeep Singh of Sri Ganganagar district.

NEW DELHI: Former Union minister P Chidambaram on Monday said the Election Commission of India (ECI)’s ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls could leave 10% of India’s eligible population — or nearly 10 crore people — without the right to vote, after a former diplomat detailed difficulties he faced establishing his citizenship during the exercise in Punjab Navdeep Suri, who served as India’s Ambassador to Egypt and the UAE and High Commissioner to Australia, questioned what the experience of a common citizen might be if he himself faced difficulties despite having represented the country in three nations.“Based on the outcomes so far, at the end of the S.I.R. process, 10% of India’s adult population will be ‘citizens’ but without the right to vote, thanks to the ECI. That is nearly 10 crore people. The ECI has created a new category of ‘non-voting citizens’,” the senior Congress leader wrote, referring to Suri’s post.Earlier, Suri said his details did not match the 2003 electoral rolls used for verification because he was posted in London at the time and had not participated in that revision.“Sharing my experience with #SIR in Punjab. Went to BLO, submitted Voter ID and Aadhaar card, was assured that everything is in order.Got a message today from a volunteer saying some details don't match with SIR in 2003!!” Suri posted on X.According to the former diplomat, officials later asked him to produce his passport as proof of citizenship.“Spoke with BLO, was told that I should come and collect the notice. And then come again with unspecified documents that show I am an Indian citizen... I happen to have documents other than voter ID and Aadhaar card.But can’t help asking: If I have trouble establishing my citizenship after representing India in three countries, what’s the fate of the common citizen? Ease of Living, I presume!” he added.Meanwhile, the Punjab Chief Electoral Officer assured citizens that receiving a notice was not a cause for concern.“As part of the ongoing SIR process, notices are being delivered to voters where required. Received a notice? Don't worry! Simply check the details, submit the required documents, and complete the process,” the Punjab CEO stated on X earlier.The draft electoral roll for Punjab was published on August 13. The state is currently undergoing the second phase of the SIR, which involves reviewing the draft electoral rolls and filing claims and objections.

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday announced a set of welfare measures in the state Assembly, including three free cooking gas cylinders a year for eligible beneficiaries and an expansion of the fare-free bus travel scheme for women.Under the cooking gas scheme, the amount for the three cylinders will be credited directly to the bank accounts of eligible beneficiaries.Vijay announced the launch of the Vetri Payanam scheme, expanding the existing fare-free bus travel programme for women across the state.Under the scheme, women will be allowed to travel free of charge on Express, LSS and Deluxe government buses operating in metropolitan and urban areas. Article Title: Parandur airport project dropped: CM Vijay backs farmers, DMK warns of economic damage
Article Text:
The Tamil Nadu government has abandoned the Parandur greenfield airport project

(With agency inputs)





CHENNAI: The Tamil Nadu government has decided to abandon steps to establish the proposed greenfield airport at Parandur, chief minister C Joseph Vijay announced in the Assembly on Monday, saying the project would affect agricultural land and disrupt the livelihoods of farmers and residents.Vijay said Chennai needs a new airport because of rising passenger traffic, industrial development and increasing cargo movement. However, he said the new airport should be located at a site where agricultural land and residential areas are minimally affected.Speaking in the Assembly, Vijay said Chennai's Meenambakkam airport, operated by the Airports Authority of India (AAI), currently has the capacity to handle around 30 million passengers annually. With Terminal 3 becoming operational, the capacity is expected to rise to 34 million passengers per year, he said.The government is also planning to construct a fifth terminal on the northwestern side of the existing airport, which Vijay said would add another 20 million passengers annually.Vijay said he had visited Eganapuram and other villages on January 20, 2025, and heard the grievances of residents protesting against the Parandur airport project."I stand firmly with the people protesting against the airport to be established in Chennai's Parandur and 12 surrounding villages," he said.Calling farmers the backbone of the country, Vijay said the government would not allow an airport project that disrupted agricultural land and people's livelihoods.He said he had opposed the Parandur project at a public meeting in Vikravandi in October 2024, while maintaining that he supported industrial development and the role of airports in promoting it."However, this project should not be located in Parandur. The government must reconsider this project," Vijay said, adding that an alternative site should be identified where minimum agricultural land was affected and people's livelihoods were not disrupted.Vijay said consultations had been held with senior officials and experts on the proposed airport."To fulfill the promise I made to the people that day... the steps taken to establish a new airport in Parandur will be abandoned by this government," he said.The chief minister said new sites were being considered and the location would be finalised soon after a technical feasibility study by expert teams.He also accused the previous DMK government of selecting a site that would require the relocation of a large number of people and affect agricultural land.The Civil Aviation Ministry had granted in-principle approval in April 2025 for setting up an international greenfield airport at Parandur in Kancheepuram district.The announcement drew sharp criticism from the opposition DMK.Former Tamil Nadu minister and DMK MLA Thangam Thennarasu said scrapping the project for political reasons would cause economic damage to the state and could prompt industries to move to neighbouring Andhra Pradesh."Possibilities for setting up two runways were all studied and only then Parandur was selected," Thennarasu told reporters.He said former chief minister MK Stalin had stated that the Parandur airport project would be dropped, but the state government had not conveyed any such decision to the Centre.Thennarasu also said compensation had already been provided to people whose land was acquired for the project."As per the Land Acquisition Act, the land acquired should be used only for the purpose for which it was acquired," he said.He maintained that Parandur was the best location for the proposed airport and warned that abandoning the project could have wider economic consequences."It would be best to have the airport at Parandur. Dropping the Parandur Airport project for political reasons will cause economic damage," Thennarasu said.He also warned that several industries could shift to Andhra Pradesh if the project was scrapped."Many industries will move towards Andhra Pradesh. We have already lost the Hosur Airport," he said.The DMK also staged a walkout from the Assembly, protesting against being denied an opportunity to speak in the House on the Parandur airport issue.The Vijay government's decision means the state will now have to identify an alternative location for Chennai's proposed second airport while expanding capacity at the existing Meenambakkam facility.
Article Summary: The Tamil Nadu government has abandoned steps to establish the proposed greenfield airport at Parandur. Chief minister C Joseph Vijay said the project would affect agricultural land and disrupt the livelihoods of farmers and residents. He said Chennai needs a new airport because of rising passenger traffic, industrial development and increasing cargo movement.

NEW DELHI: Heavy rain lashed Delhi-NCR on Monday, causing widespread waterlogging, traffic snarls and flight disruptions, with 15 Delhi-bound flights diverted.Fifteen flights Delhi-bound flights diverted, including two international flights, with 11 diverted to Jaipur. Passengers have been advised to check with their respective airlines for the latest flight updates.The weather office issued red and orange alerts for heavy to moderate rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms and winds of up to 40 kmph.Heavy rain and thunderstorms were witnessed at isolated places in South East Delhi, East Delhi, Shahdara, Central Delhi, North East Delhi, South Delhi, New Delhi, South West Delhi, West Delhi, North West Delhi and North Delhi.Between 8.30am and 11.30am, Chhatarpur recorded the highest rainfall in Delhi at 28mm, followed by Lodi Road at 24.6mm and Pitampura at 18.5mm, according to the IMD.The Ridge recorded 5mm of rainfall, Mayur Vihar 1.5mm, Safdarjung 1mm and Ayanagar 0.1mm during the period.The showers were accompanied by strong winds in several areas, with waterlogging reported around New Ashok Nagar Metro Station, Burari, C R Park and Alaknanda.Commuters took to social media to share visuals of waterlogged roads and traffic disruptions. Commuters were seen wading through the flooded Zakhira underpass, while rainwater accumulated in a parking lot at Connaught Place.Students navigated severely waterlogged streets in Sangam Vihar, and children were seen swimming and playing on inundated roads in Durga Vihar.Waterlogging was also reported from Gurugram's Sector 46 and several locations in Noida, including Sector 95.Delhi recorded a minimum temperature of 27.8 degrees Celsius at Safdarjung on Monday, 1.4 degrees above normal. The Ridge recorded the lowest minimum temperature in the city at 24 degrees Celsius.Air India advised passengers travelling to and from Delhi to check their flight status before heading to the airport, warning that adverse weather could impact flight operations.IndiGo also issued a travel advisory, saying bad weather over Delhi had affected flight schedules. The airline urged passengers to check their flight status on its website or app before leaving for the airport and advised them to allow additional travel time as road conditions could be slower than usual.(With Agency Inputs)
Article Summary: 15 Delhi-bound flights diverted, including two international flights, with 11 diverted to Jaipur. Article Title: In a first, Census 2027 will not record data on begging
Article Text:
The number of beggars in the country will no longer figure in census tables.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a departure from previous exercises, Census 2027 will not record data on begging separately, with the questionnaire having omitted the category 'beggars and vagrants etc' from the list of 'non-economic activity'. This, as per sources, is due to the very less return in this category in the last census; just around 3.8 lakh non-workers and marginal workers declared themselves as 'beggars and vagrants' in Census 2011.Another key change in is the inclusion of 'natural calamities' as a 'reason for migration', in addition to work, business, education, marriage, moved after birth, moved with household and 'any other'.While the 2011 census and earlier had listed 'beggars and vagrants etc' as marginal and non-workers engaged in 'non-economic activity' - in addition to students, household duties, dependents, pensioners, rentiers and others - they will now be counted among 'others'; as a result, the number of beggars in the country or their classification by age, religion, state/UT, educational status etc will no longer figure in census tables.Sources said the count of 'beggars and vagrants' returned by previous census exercises was not considered reliable, as many respondents in this category were reluctant to return themselves as such due to associated social stigma. "Census rules require the enumerator to record the occupation/non-economic activity as declared by the respondent," an officer said. The count of non-worker beggars/vagrants was thus recorded at around 3.8 lakh in Census 2011, 6.3 lakh in Census 2001 and around 5.4 lakh in Census 1991.As for the new census fields 'father's particulars' and 'mother's particulars' - which will capture date and place of their birth as well as religion - sources said they need to be filled only where the mother and father are not listed in the same household or are no longer alive. The enumeration form already records the religion and date and place of birth of each member of the census household, including parents.Sources told TOI that some of the trends that may emerge from recording religion of both parents include generation-wise prevalence of inter-faith marriages and history of religious conversion. Also, date and place of birth of parents will give the aggregate data on how many Indians fulfil citizenship criteria as per Citizenship Act.While the latest questionnaire seeks details like mobile number, Aadhaar, voter ID and Indian passport number, where "available", technically requiring every individual having these documents to share their number, sources said the enumerators have been trained to only persuade the respondents to do so, by assuring them that all individual data will remain confidential. If the respondent is still reluctant, the enumerator shall leave these fields empty."Even blank fields will enable the census team to cull out data on which of the documents - Aadhaar, voter ID and passport number - respondents are most reluctant to share due to privacy concerns," an official told TOI.
Article Summary: In a departure from previous exercises, Census 2027 will not record data on begging separately. This is due to the very less return in this category in the last census. Just around 3.8 lakh non-workers and marginal workers declared themselves as 'beggars and vagrants' in Census 2011.

Article Title: Donald Trump's volatility may have made India decline G7 presser
Article Text:
‘Unpredictable’ Trump behind no press conference after PM Modi meeting, govt says

NEW DELHI: Govt justified its decision not to have a news conference after PM Modi's meeting with President Donald Trump on the margins of the G7 summit in France, with official sources citing Trump's "unpredictable behaviour" at media events that have followed his meetings with heads of state/govt, including from South Africa and Ukraine.US ambassador to India Sergio Gor had earlier created a stir with his remarks about how ministry of external affairs had called to limit media interaction to photo opportunities and opening remarks without taking questions. Despite the request from MEA, as Gor had said, Trump went on to have a 45-minute unscripted news conference at the media event. Govt sources here stressed there was no unusual demand made by the Indian side.According to Gor, while MEA wanted to bring in the media, it said, "let's not do a full news conference".The ambassador’s disclosure of what might have been a private discussion is learned to have upset the govt. “Discussions regarding arrangements for public appearances of leaders are normal practice ahead of any VVIP visit,” said a govt source, on condition of anonymity. “Delegations when meeting Donald Trump are wary about his unpredictable behaviour, as may be seen from his interactions with president of South Africa, Ukraine, etc.Thus, the cautious approach by India,” he added.In highlighting Trump’s previous interactions with the presidents of Ukraine and S Africa, which devolved into televised confrontations with Trump hectoring his visitors, govt sources framed India’s request as a necessary safeguard against unpredictable diplomatic settings. The standard practice for govt has been to not have unscripted joint news conferences by Modi in company of the host or visiting dignitaries.This practice, though, has been questioned by local journalists recently in countries like Norway, the Netherlands, Australia and New Zealand.MEA defended the arrangement, stating that standard diplomatic procedures for international visits are followed.
Article Summary: US ambassador to India had earlier created a stir with his remarks about how ministry of external affairs had called to limit media interaction to photo opportunities and opening remarks without taking questions. Despite the request from MEA, as Sergio Gor had said, Trump went on to have a 45-minute unscripted news conference at the media event.

Article Title: 20 Blackbucks rewilded in Banni Grasslands on India’s 80th Independence Day by Anant Ambani’s Vantara
Article Text:
Part of a wider Gujarat Native Herbivore Conservation Programme

On India’s 80th Independence Day, the Gujarat Forest Department, with technical support from Greens Zoological Rescue and Rehabilitation Centre (GZRRC), Vantara, released 20 blackbucks also known as antilope cervicapra, into the Banni Grasslands of Kutch, marking an important milestone in the restoration of native wildlife and the ecological character of this unique grassland landscape.The release comprised five male and 15 female blackbucks, transferred from Vantara, Jamnagar, following the requisite approvals of the Chief Wildlife Warden, Gujarat, and the Central Zoo Authority (CZA). The transfer was undertaken in accordance with prescribed protocols covering veterinary examination, health screening, quarantine, disease surveillance, safe and humane transportation and release. Vantara complied with all the necessary requirements.The significance of the initiative extends beyond the release of 20 animals. Restoring native herbivores is an important part of rebuilding the ecological fabric of Banni, strengthening its native herbivore community, supporting natural predator prey relationships and contributing to the recovery of a more resilient grassland ecosystem.Banni is a vast grassland landscape supporting pastoral communities and diverse native wildlife. Blackbuck, chinkara, nilgai and wild boar have historically formed part of its herbivore assemblage. Their recovery, alongside habitat conservation and scientific grassland management, can help restore the ecological character and biodiversity of the landscape.The initiative reflects the broader national commitment to the revival of India’s native species and restoration of its grassland ecosystems, a conservation direction strongly championed under the leadership of the Hon’ble Prime Minister of India, Narendra Modi.Dr Jaipal Singh, IFS, Chief Wildlife Warden, Gujarat, said, “Restoring native wildlife is fundamental to restoring healthy landscapes. The release of these 20 blackbucks into Banni on India’s Independence Day is an important milestone in our continuing effort to recover the ecological character and biodiversity of this unique grasslands. Such restoration requires science, sustained management and collaboration, and we appreciate Vantara’s technical support in carrying out the programme in accordance with prescribed protocols. ”Ajit Kulkarni, Special Director, Compliance & Due Diligence, Vantara, said, “There can be no greater privilege on Independence Day than contributing to a future in which India’s native species continue to live and flourish in the natural landscapes to which they belong. Species restoration is not simply about releasing animals; it requires a thorough understanding of the habitat, the species and the individual animals being released, as well as habitat dynamics, population planning, and the active support of all stakeholders, particularly local communities, to ensure the long term success and sustainability of these efforts. We are honoured to support the Gujarat Forest Department and the Government’s conservation vision for Banni, and to contribute our technical capabilities wherever they can strengthen India’s wildlife conservation efforts.”The Banni release forms part of a wider programme to strengthen native herbivore populations across Gujarat. The Central Government, through the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, has approved the translocation of 500 blackbucks and 100 chinkara, with the Chief Wildlife Warden, Gujarat, providing the necessary directions for the exercise.While components of this wider programme support prey base augmentation in connection with the planned cheetah reintroduction programme, the Banni blackbuck release also has an important and independent species restoration objective: rebuilding populations of wildlife native to the grasslands.The Banni Grassland Forest Division has sought Vantara’s technical support for the wider translocation programme, including specialised herbivore transport vehicles, portable boma systems, veterinary expertise and technical support for safe handling and transportation.The initiative builds on the Gujarat Forest Department’s sustained conservation work. With the approval of the Chief Wildlife Warden, Gujarat, Vantara has previously supported the Forest Department in the rewilding of nearly 80 spotted deer in Barda Wildlife Sanctuary, contributing to biodiversity strengthening within the Asiatic lion conservation landscape.
Article Summary: 20 blackbucks were released into the Banni Grasslands of Kutch. The release is part of a wider programme to strengthen native herbivore populations. The initiative reflects the broader national commitment to the revival of India’s native species and restoration of its grassland ecosystems.

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday announced that his government would abandon the proposed greenfield airport project at Parandur, saying the project would affect agricultural land and disrupt the livelihoods of farmers and residents.The announcement was made in the assembly as Vijay said Chennai still needed a new airport to meet rising passenger demand, industrial growth and increasing cargo movement. However, he said the new airport should be located at a site where agricultural and residential areas would face minimal disruption."To fulfill the promise I made to the people that day... the steps taken to establish a new airport in Parandur will be abandoned by this government," Vijay said.The government is now considering alternative locations and plans to conduct technical feasibility studies before finalising a new site.Vijay said he had visited Eganapuram and other villages on January 20, 2025, and heard the grievances of residents protesting against the proposed airport in Parandur and 12 surrounding villages."I stand firmly with the people protesting against the airport to be established in Chennai's Parandur and 12 surrounding villages," he said.The chief minister said farmers were the backbone of the country and backed those protesting to protect their agricultural land.Vijay said he had also opposed the Parandur project at a public meeting in Vikravandi in October 2024, while making clear that he supported industrial development and the role of airports in it."However, this project should not be located in Parandur. The government must reconsider this project," he said.He added that an alternative site should be identified where the impact on agricultural land and people's livelihoods would be minimal.While dropping Parandur, the government said Chennai's existing airport would be expanded.Vijay said the Meenambakkam airport, operated by the Airports Authority of India, currently has the capacity to handle around 30 million passengers annually. With the under-construction Terminal 3 becoming operational, capacity is expected to rise to 34 million passengers a year.The government plans to expand the airport on its north-western side by constructing a fifth terminal, which is expected to handle another 20 million passengers annually.The government is also considering alternative sites for a new airport, with technical feasibility studies to be conducted by expert teams.The Parandur project had received in-principle approval from the Civil Aviation Ministry in April 2025 for an International Greenfield Airport in Kancheepuram district.The proposed project had faced opposition from residents of villages that were expected to be affected by land acquisition and construction.However, the DMK has criticised the decision to abandon the project, arguing that it could hurt Tamil Nadu's industrial growth and investment prospects.Former chief minister and DMK president MK Stalin said dropping the project would set the state's development back by several years."The announcement made today by the Hon'ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu to drop the Parandur International Airport project will set the state's development back by several years. Tamil Nadu's interests cannot be mortgaged for petty political considerations," Stalin said.He also called the decision a setback to employment opportunities for Tamil Nadu's youth.Former Tamil Nadu minister and DMK MLA Thangam Thennarasu also criticised the decision, saying the Parandur site was selected after studying options for establishing two runways."Possibilities for setting up two runways were all studied and only then Parandur was selected," he said.Thennarasu argued that scrapping the project for political reasons could hurt the state's economy and push industries towards neighbouring Andhra Pradesh."It would be best to have the airport at Parandur. Dropping the Parandur Airport project for political reasons will cause economic damage," he said."Many industries will move towards Andhra Pradesh. We have already lost the Hosur Airport," he added.Thennarasu also said compensation had already been provided to people whose land was acquired for the project and cited the Land Acquisition Act while arguing that the acquired land should be used for its intended purpose.The announcement triggered an immediate confrontation in the Tamil Nadu Assembly, with DMK MLAs staging a walkout after Speaker JCD Prabhakar denied DMK leader KN Nehru permission to respond to the statement, citing Assembly rules.The opposition accused the government of making a policy U-turn that could affect Tamil Nadu's industrial momentum and prospects of attracting investment.Vijay, however, maintained that the government supports airport-led industrial development but believes the proposed airport should not come at the cost of agricultural land and people's livelihoods.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay announced that his government would abandon the proposed greenfield airport project at Parandur. Vijay said the project would affect agricultural land and disrupt the livelihoods of farmers and residents. The government is now considering alternative locations and plans to conduct technical feasibility studies.

NEW DELHI: Expanding the list of well-documented and scientifically recognised animal breeds in the country, the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) has registered 16 more new breeds of indigenous animals including cattle and buffalo, taking the total number of such breeds in India to 262. The move will help in conservation and sustainable utilisation of India’s diverse and climate-resilient animal genetic resources at a time when rising temperature due to global warming is posing grave risk to animal productivity and the overall food security.The new indigenous breeds include four each of cattle (Umarda, Periyar, Koppal and Mahakaushali) and Sheep (Madgyal, Seemanchali, Kow Debar and Asomi); two goats (Totapuri and Battisi); and one each of buffalo (Gomanchali), dog (Kombai), pig (Nagal), horse/pony (Kashmiri), donkey (Braj) and yak (Sikkimese yak).These breeds, registered early this month, represent diverse agro-ecological regions spreading across 13 states -- Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Kerala, Maharashtra, Goa, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Assam, Uttarakhand, Bihar, Nagaland, Sikkim and Tamil Nadu -- and UT of Jammu & Kashmir. Goat breed Battisi is distributed across Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh whereas the sheep breed Madgyal is found in Maharashtra and Karnataka."Indigenous breeds have evolved under diverse production environments and possess locally adapted characteristics that can be valuable for climate resilience, disease adaptation, low-input production, livelihood support and sustainable livestock farming. Their conservation is therefore important not only for maintaining genetic diversity but also for ensuring the availability of adaptive livestock resources for future generations," N H Mohan, directorof the ICAR's National Bureau of Animal Genetic Resources (NBAGR), toldKarnal-based ICAR-NBAGR is the nodal institute for registration of livestock and poultry breeds in India. With the new addition, the indigenous animal breeds now include 59 for cattle (Sahiwal, Gir, Red Kandhari and Hallikar etc.) 23 for buffalo (Murrah, Nili Ravi, Bhadawari and Mehsana etc.), 45 for goat, 50 for sheep, 16 for pigs, nine each for horses & ponies, camel and duck; five for donkey; six for dog and three for yak among others."The new registrations strengthen the national effort to reduce the proportion of nondescript livestock populations through systematic breed identification and documentation. This approach is particularly important for ensuring that valuable locally adapted populations are scientifically recognized and brought within appropriate conservation and sustainable utilization programmes," said Mohan.He said, "ICAR-NBAGR's efforts are aligned with the broader national objective of strengthening India's livestock genetic base and supporting food and nutritional security, sustainable livelihoods and climate-resilient livestock production."
Article Summary: The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) has registered 16 more new breeds of indigenous animals including cattle and buffalo. The move will help in conservation and sustainable utilisation of India’s diverse and climate- resilient animal genetic resources. Rising temperature due to global warming is posing grave risk to animal productivity and the overall food security.

Article Title: Govt seeks generation data from rooftop solar
Article Text:
Rooftop solar (RTS) systems under the PM Surya Ghar scheme. Photo credit : PTI

NEW DELHI: As the number of households installing rooftop solar (RTS) systems under the PM Surya Ghar scheme rises and renewable energy capacity increases, govt has decided to track how much electricity these systems are actually generating, with inverter makers required to share daily generation data with the national portal.The move could give govt, for the first time, a system to monitor the performance of individual RTS installations rather than merely track the capacity added under the scheme.Under new guidelines issued by the ministry of new and renewable energy, inverter manufacturers will have to provide daily cumulative generation data through an API to the national portal, mapped to the device’s serial number. The guidelines also require applications, monitoring and control servers and cloud-hosted data linked to inverter systems to be located in India.The data could help govt assess how much electricity rooftop systems are actually generating and identify under-performing installations. It could also allow generation to be analysed across states and power distribution companies (discoms), providing a clearer picture of the energy benefits being delivered by the scheme.A govt-appointed Expert Committee on Energy Statistics also flagged the absence of comprehensive data on electricity generated and consumed by decentralised renewable energy systems in a recent report.Currently, more than 44 lakh RTS systems have been installed under the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana (PMSGMBY), benefiting over 52 lakh households and adding 15.6 GW of solar capacity.The committee noted that electricity generated by rooftop solar systems is often consumed at the premises and does not pass through the grid, leaving it outside conventional electricity supply statistics. It said generation, export and self-consumption data from rooftop systems are not uniformly recorded or aggregated by discoms and recommended mandatory collection and reporting of such data to improve the accuracy of India’s electricity statistics.“Electricity generated from many of these systems is already metered. However, these meter readings are either not visible to the discoms or, even if they are visible, the readings are not recorded systematically and reported,” the committee said.Alekhya Datta, director, electricity and renewables division, TERI, said national-level centralised monitoring of electricity generation from rooftop solar systems would have multiple benefits. “If electricity distribution companies have data on electricity generated by rooftop solar plants (behind the meter) in their respective areas and the units consumed by consumers, they will be able to plan their power purchases accordingly,” Datta said.“The amount of electricity generated by RTS plants will also give an indication of the quality of the system, and this attribute can be used in a vendor rating system as well as help improve operations and maintenance. Consumers, too, will get a sense of satisfaction from knowing their contribution to the environment.”Though the ministry has asked all inverter companies to share daily generation data, Datta said only around 15 per cent of inverters currently have the capability to share it through APIs. The govt is also yet to create an integrated dashboard where the data can be collated.
Article Summary: The move could give govt, for the first time, a system to monitor the performance of individual RTS installations. More than 44 lakh RTS systems have been installed under the PM Surya Ghar scheme. Data could help govt assess how much electricity rooftop systems are actually generating.

NEW DELHI: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leader Arvind Kejriwal will address a town hall on E20 petrol policy during his two-day visit to Goa beginning Monday.Kejriwal landed at Dabolim Airport in south Goa on Sunday, where he was received by local party leaders.AAP sources said Kejriwal would address a press conference on Monday in Panaji and a town hall a day later on E20 petrol policy.The AAP, which has two MLAs in the 40-member Goa assembly, has announced a campaign against the "forced implementation" of E20 (ethanol-blended) fuel in the coastal state, which will go to polls in 2027.Earlier this month, Kejriwal had demanded the government give the option to choose between pure petrol and E20 at fuel pumps.The Centre introduced E20, a blend of 20 per cent ethanol and 80 per cent petrol, as part of efforts to reduce vehicular emissions and cut dependence on crude oil imports. NEW DELHI: Trying to accelerate the adoption of piped gas for cooking and industrial purposes, the Centre has asked states and Union Territories to provide district-level administrative support and appoint nodal officers to coordinate with gas distributors and oil marketing companies to expand the network.Govt has also directed authorised city gas distribution companies and public sector oil marketing companies to establish PNG coordination committees to identify eligible housing societies and households and conduct outreach camps to accelerate piped gas connections.In a letter to state chief secretaries, petroleum secretary Neeraj Mittal said PNG was crucial for India’s energy transition and could help reduce dependence on cooking gas cylinders.“PNG brings a safer, cleaner and more efficient cooking fuel, playing a critical role in advancing the country’s energy transition objectives. Its accelerated adoption contributes to reducing the logistics burden associated with LPG distribution, enhancing consumer convenience, and improving utilisation of CGD infrastructure created through substantial public and private investment,” Mittal said in the letter.While the potential for PNG is huge, its adoption so far has not matched the govt’s expectations. During the West Asia conflict, when energy supplies were disrupted and an LPG shortage loomed large, govt made concerted efforts to push PNG adoption by seeking the help of states and UTs and easing the regulatory framework for faster laying of pipeline networks. Govt is also trying to prevent households from retaining both LPG and PNG connections in areas where piped gas is available.Officials said administrative support at the district level was vital for securing right of way or right of use in housing societies, supporting consumer outreach and verification, and resolving consumer grievances.Mittal has also asked chief secretaries to direct their respective food and civil supplies departments to nominate one nodal officer at the district level to be associated with the local PCC.

Article Title: Digital financial inclusion key to boosting women's participation in India’s platform economy: ILO-NCAER
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Despite the flexibility offered by platform work, women’s participation in India’s growing platform economy remains constrained by limited access to formal financial services, gaps in digital literacy, safety concerns and restrictive social norms, an ILO-NCAER policy brief said on Monday.The brief, “Advancing Women’s Digital Financial Inclusion in the Platform Economy”, said women need access to a range of financial services throughout their platform-work journey, including start-up capital, short-term credit, insurance, savings and financial planning tools.It highlighted cashflow-based lending as a key lever for inclusion, particularly because women are less likely to own land or property that can be used as collateral. Digital records of platform payments can provide lenders with verifiable evidence of income and repayment capacity.Addressing a Roundtable at the release of the Policy Brief, NCAER director general Suresh Goyal said, “A woman’s best protection is a little money of her own and access to credit and mobility are important conditions for women to have better employment opportunities. Platform economy has given that opportunity.”The brief identified two ways to leverage women’s digital footprints: using India’s Digital Public Infrastructure, including the Account Aggregator framework, to make financial data portable, and enabling platforms to partner with lenders to offer loans, savings and insurance through their apps.ILO country director Michiko Miyamoto said, “Digital financial inclusion must enable women to build income security, resilience, and sustainable livelihoods."ILO Senior Specialist Radhicka Kapoor said integrating financial DPI with e-Shram records could further expand access, provided safeguards against algorithmic bias are built in.The brief also flagged device ownership as a barrier, noting that women’s digital access is often mediated through family members.NITI Aayog estimates India’s platform workforce could rise from 12 million in 2024-25 to 23.5 million by 2029-30.Director of NCAER’s Centre for Gender and Macroeconomy, Prof. Ratna Sahay, summed up the key takeaway, “Digital footprint in platform economies can be a game-changer for women to access credit, underpinned by regulation that encourages innovation while ensuring consumer protection and financial stability.”
Article Summary: NITI Aayog estimates India’s platform workforce could rise from 12 million in 2024-25 to 23.5 million by 2029-30. Women need access to a range of financial services throughout their platform-work journey. Cashflow-based lending is a key lever for inclusion.

NEW DELHI: India's national security adviser Ajit Doval arrived in Beijing on Monday for a two-day visit. He is set to hold the 25th round of Special Representatives' Talks on the India-China boundary question with Chinese foreign minister Wang Yi on Tuesday. The visit comes as New Delhi and Beijing seek to build on recent signs of a thaw in ties.The ministry of external affairs (MEA) said Doval arrived in Beijing "at the invitation of Wang Yi".The talks come amid efforts by the two sides to gradually normalise relations following years of tensions along their disputed Himalayan border."The NSA will also call on China's vice president Han Zheng during his visit," the MEA said.The central focus of the talks will be the unresolved India-China boundary issues, with both sides expected to discuss the management of differences and the preservation of peace and tranquillity along the Line of Actual Control.Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said the two sides would continue discussions in accordance with agreements reached by their leaders.India and China share a roughly 3,500-kilometre disputed border.Relations came under severe strain after the deadly military clash in eastern Ladakh in 2020, following which the two sides held repeated military and diplomatic talks to address the situation.The latest Special Representatives’ meeting comes against the backdrop of a broader effort to stabilise the relationship.Doval's Beijing visit follows his meeting with Wang in New Delhi in June on the sidelines of the BRICS National Security Advisers' meeting.The MEA described those discussions as part of the process of rebuilding bilateral ties.According to MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal, the two sides "reviewed recent developments in bilateral relations and noted progress towards gradual normalisation".Jaiswal said Doval had stressed the importance of maintaining a stable relationship."NSA underlined that stable, predictable and constructive bilateral relations contribute to building trust and better understanding between the two sides," he said, adding: "The discussions were constructive and forward-looking."The latest visit also comes after subsequent meetings between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese president Xi Jinping on the sidelines of major international summits.At the SCO Summit in Tianjin last year, PM Modi and Xi welcomed what the two sides described as positive momentum and steady progress in bilateral relations following their previous meeting in Kazan in October 2024.The two leaders had also reaffirmed that India and China were development partners rather than rivals, and that differences between them should not be allowed to become disputes."A stable relationship and cooperation between India and China and their 2.8 billion peoples on the basis of mutual respect, mutual interest and mutual sensitivity are necessary for the growth and development of the two countries, as well as for a multipolar world and a multi-polar Asia befitting the trends of the 21st century," the MEA had said in a statement after the leaders' meeting.The Special Representatives’ mechanism has been one of the key diplomatic channels for addressing the boundary dispute between India and China. The 25th round comes at a time when both governments are seeking to consolidate the recent improvement in relations without setting aside their differences over the border.For New Delhi, maintaining a stable and predictable relationship with Beijing is also significant as India prepares for the BRICS summit next month, where it hopes Xi will attend.
Article Summary: India's national security adviser Ajit Doval arrived in Beijing on Monday for a two-day visit. Article Title: Change in revenue record doesn't create, end property title: SC
Article Text:
SC clarifies property mutation only serves revenue purposes, cannot by itself establish or extinguish ownership rights

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Observing that mutation of a property in revenue records does not create or extinguish ownership, Supreme Court has said that title of property cannot be decided on the sole basis of revenue record and it must be weighed along with other evidence.A bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and Augustine George Masih quashed the order of Madhya Pradesh HC which decided a title dispute on the basis of the revenue record. It said a right in immovable property cannot be treated as having been voluntarily abandoned because of a revenue entry in favour of another person. It must be independently established by the party relying on it.The bench said,“It is settled law that an entry in the revenue record neither creates nor extinguishes title and exists essentially for fiscal purposes. The order of the naib tehsildar may regulate the revenue record, but it cannot, merely by recording one person’s name in place of another, operate as a conveyance or a relinquishment of proprietary rights, and the civil court remains fully competent to determine the underlying title, which the revenue entry follows .“The statutory presumption of correctness attaching to a revenue entry under Section 117 of the MP Land Revenue Code, 1959, is a rebuttable evidentiary presumption and not a presumption of title, and it must be weighed along with the rest of the evidence.”It said mutation of a property in revenue record does not create or extinguish title nor has it any presumptive value and it only enables the person in whose favour mutation is ordered to pay the land revenue in question. SC said the starting point of the limitation can’t be fixed merely by identifying the date on which the revenue entry was made.
Article Summary: Justices Sanjay Karol and Augustine George Masih quashed order of Madhya Pradesh HC which decided a title dispute on the basis of the revenue record. It said a right in immovable property cannot be treated as having been voluntarily abandoned because of a revenue entry in favour of another person.

Article Title: CM Dhami says government is committed to making women, youth and rural entrepreneurs self-reliant

Chief minister Shri Pushkar Singh Dhami on Friday inaugurated Chaupal–2026 under the “Chief Minister’s Udyamshala Yojana” at the Mukhya Sevak Sadan located at the chief minister’s Camp Office. On the occasion, he said that more than 13,000 entrepreneurs across the state have so far been supported through the Chief Minister’s Udyamshala Yojana. In addition, more than 8,000 women entrepreneurs and members of Self-Help Groups have been connected with entrepreneurship and livelihood opportunities.During the inaugural session, the chief minister announced that a state-level marketing centre would be established at 13 Gaon in IT Park, Dehradun, to facilitate the marketing of products made by Self-Help Groups from all districts of Uttarakhand.Addressing the inaugural session, the chief minister said that today, the villages of Uttarakhand are not only becoming participants in the development of the state but are also playing an important role in building a self-reliant Uttarakhand through their capabilities and hard work. He said that the enthusiastic youth and enterprising women of the state possess the desire and skills to achieve something meaningful, while Uttarakhand’s local products have immense potential to reach markets across the country and the world.What is needed is to provide the right direction to this talent.With this vision, the state government has been working to take the “Chief Minister’s Udyamshala Yojana” forward. Through the scheme, the government aims to ensure that the youth of Uttarakhand become job creators rather than job seekers. At the same time, efforts are being made to strengthen the economic condition of farmers and women. The Chief Minister’s Udyamshala Yojana is an important means of translating this vision into reality.He said that through the scheme, rural entrepreneurs are being provided with the necessary training, financial assistance, technical guidance and support in connecting with markets to start and expand their businesses.The chief minister said that on the one hand, more than 5 lakh rural women in the state have been connected with over 70,000 Self-Help Groups through the National Rural Livelihood Mission. On the other hand, more than 3 lakh women have successfully become Lakhpati Didis. He said that the women of Uttarakhand are turning everything from hill spices, mandua (finger millet), jhangora (barnyard millet), pulses, honey, pickles and jams to handicrafts, woollen products and local art into successful enterprises.The chief minister said that the government is working to take products made in villages to major cities across the country. In this direction, an umbrella brand named House of Himalayas has been created.He said that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has given the nation the mantras of Vocal for Local, Local to Global and Atmanirbhar Bharat. The state government is working to translate these mantras into reality. The government wants that whenever someone purchases a product from Uttarakhand, they should also experience the hard work, culture, traditions and fragrance of the soil of the hills in that product.For this reason, facilities such as rural haats, marketing centres, collection centres and agriculture service centres are being strengthened across the state so that farmers and entrepreneurs can access better markets and receive better prices for their products.He said that a major objective of promoting rural entrepreneurship is also to check migration from the hills. The government wants young people to not be compelled to leave their villages in search of employment. Because when villages become strong, Uttarakhand becomes strong.In this direction, the government is also working through the Gramothan Project (REAP) to connect extremely poor families in villages with livelihood opportunities and increase employment opportunities in rural areas.The chief minister said that “Chief Minister’s Udyamshala Chaupals” are being organised in all 13 districts of the state. The objective of these chaupals is to ensure that more and more people become aware of government schemes and are able to benefit from them. For the same purpose, publicity vans are also being sent to villages so that information about the Chief Minister’s Udyamshala Yojana reaches the last person in society.During the programme, the chief minister felicitated Lakhpati Didis and women entrepreneurs. He also released a book and annual report prepared under the Uttarakhand State Rural Livelihood Mission. In addition, he launched the Integrated Agriculture Cluster Basic Training and Module, the Infant and Young Child Feeding Module, and the Module on Prevention and Management of Anaemia among Women and Children.Cabinet Ministers Shri Bharat Chaudhary, Shri Ganesh Joshi and Shri Khajan Das, Rajya Sabha MP Shri Naresh Bansal, MLAs Shri Umesh Sharma Kau and Smt. Savita Kapoor, Secretary Rural Development Shri Dheeraj Garbyal, and other concerned officials were present on the occasion.
Article Summary: Chief minister Shri Pushkar Singh Dhami on Friday inaugurated Chaupal–2026 under the “Chief Minister’s Udyamshala Yojana’ The chief minister announced that a state-level marketing centre would be established at 13 Gaon in IT Park, Dehradun, to facilitate the marketing of products made by Self-Help Groups.

CHENNAI: The Tamil Nadu government has dropped the proposed greenfield airport project at Parandur, chief minister C Joseph Vijay announced in the Assembly on Monday.The chief minister, while making announcements under Section 110, said new sites were being considered for the proposed airport and the location would be finalised soon. Article Title: Delhi government orders construction ban for 42 days to tackle winter air pollution
Article Text:
File photo: Delhi air pollution (PTI photo)

AI cameras to monitor construction sites

What is Delhi's AI-powered Dust Portal?

NEW DELHI: Construction activities in Delhi will be completely banned from December 10 to January 20 as part of the government's measures to control air pollution during the winter season, chief minister Rekha Gupta said on Friday.In a post on X, Gupta urged people to report violations, saying construction sites measuring more than 500 square metres would be monitored through the Delhi government's Dust Portal and AI-enabled cameras.“Construction will be completely banned from 10 December to 20 January. If you spot any violation, inform MCD, your MLA, or me directly,” Gupta said.Gupta said construction had continued at some sites during the previous winter despite the implementation of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP), with work being carried out behind covers.“Last time, even under GRAP, some construction continued behind covers,” she said.This year, such sites will be monitored in real time through the Dust Portal and AI-enabled cameras. Alerts generated by the system will be sent to the government's Control and Command Centre, Gupta said.“Notices, warnings and fines will follow,” she wrote, urging people to “inform, tag, complain and stop them”.The Delhi government launched Dust Portal 2.0 in July to strengthen monitoring of construction and demolition sites and improve enforcement of dust pollution-control measures.The portal, developed by the Delhi Pollution Control Committee, integrates GIS mapping, live 360-degree PTZ cameras, PM10 and PM2.5 sensors and AI-based analytics to monitor compliance at construction sites measuring 500 square yards or more.The system generates yellow, orange and red alerts based on pollution levels and enables digital issuance of compliance certificates and enforcement notices when violations are detected.The upgraded portal also provides dashboards for district-wise monitoring, pollution trends and hotspot analysis.Officials and project proponents can remotely monitor construction sites through live camera feeds, sensor data and AI-generated analysis, according to news agency PTI.
Article Summary: Construction activities in Delhi will be completely banned from December 10 to January 20. Chief minister Rekha Gupta urged people to report violations. Construction sites measuring more than 500 square metres will be monitored through the Delhi government's Dust Portal and AI-enabled cameras.

Article Title: How Travis Kelce is securing his future with a $100 million business empire beyond the Chiefs and building a fortune designed to last long after football
Article Text:
Travis Kelce (Image via Getty)

How Travis Kelce is building his $100 million business empire beyond the Chiefs

Travis Kelce (Getty ​Images)

New Heights

Travis Kelce’s investments could shape his life after football

Travis Kelce (Getty Images)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Travis Kelce has spent more than a decade turning Sundays into a career worth remembering. Now, his biggest plays are happening away from the football field. With a reported fortune approaching $100 million, the Kansas City Chiefs star has built a growing portfolio across media, investments, endorsements, food and sports ownership. His strategy is clear: create income streams and business relationships that can keep working even when his NFL career eventually ends.Kelce’s financial story is no longer tied only to his NFL paycheck. His career earnings from football have surpassed $111 million, but his off-field opportunities have become a major part of his financial picture. Forbes has estimated that he earned about $30 million off the field in 2025, including advertising and podcast income.The biggest piece of that media strategy is, the podcast Kelce hosts with his brother Jason. Amazon’s Wondery signed the brothers to a deal reportedly worth more than $100 million, giving the podcast a much larger commercial platform. That agreement matters because it turns their personalities and family chemistry into a long-term media asset rather than a side project.Kelce has also taken a hands-on approach to investing. His portfolio includes consumer brands and companies spanning beverages, fitness, food and lifestyle.His investment in Sleep Number is one recent example. He acquired a stake of less than 5% and became a brand spokesperson, combining ownership with a role that can increase his commercial value.That approach says plenty about how Kelce sees business. He is not simply attaching his name to products. In several cases, he is putting money behind companies and using his enormous audience to help them grow.Perhaps the most personal addition to Kelce’s portfolio came in May 2026, when he joined the ownership group of the Cleveland Guardians as a minority investor. For the Cleveland Heights native, the move carried more meaning than a financial investment. It connected him with the professional sports community of the city where he grew up.He has also invested alongside Jason in Garage Beer. The company reached a reported $200 million valuation after securing institutional backing, giving the brothers another significant business interest outside the NFL.Kelce’s business interests now stretch across entertainment, consumer products and professional sports. That diversification could prove especially valuable as he approaches the later stages of his playing career.The NFL will eventually ask Kelce to walk away. His business portfolio does not have to.That may be the most important part of his financial strategy. He is using the fame created by football to build assets that do not depend entirely on football. And if the reported $100 million figure continues to grow, Kelce could enter retirement with something more valuable than a collection of NFL records: a business platform capable of carrying his name into an entirely new chapter.
Article Summary: Travis Kelce has built a growing portfolio across media, investments, endorsements, food and sports ownership. Kelce’s financial story is no longer tied only to his NFL paycheck. Forbes has estimated that he earned about $30 million off the field in 2025, including advertising and podcast income.

Article Title: Delhi H1N1 surge: Experts urge caution, advise avoiding crowds; higher risk for children, elderly
Article Text:
Delhi sees an increase in H1N1 cases, prompting expert advice for precautions





NEW DELHI: With H1N1 cases increasing in Delhi, doctors have urged people to take precautions, stay away from crowded places when symptomatic and remain particularly alert if children or people with underlying health conditions develop flu-like symptoms.Dr Dhiren Gupta, senior paediatrician and co-director, Paediatric Pulmonology, Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, said children who develop a cough or cold should ideally not go to school or mix with groups to help prevent the spread of infection.He said children and people with comorbidities are at greater risk of complications."Those with comorbidities, such as diabetes, hypertension, chronic lung disease, asthma, or neurological issues, are at the highest risk. So, it is our duty to do everything we can to curb the spread within the community."Gupta said the current virus was causing more distress among children under five, while high fever was particularly troubling those below two years."About 70% of the cases are H1N1, which we know as Swine Flu. Compared to the initial outbreak in 2009, the virus is causing more distress in children under five, while high fever is troubling those under two...Problems mostly arise in children with underlying health conditions or those under two years of age, specifically those who stop eating or drinking and develop high fevers of 103°F or 104°F. This is an antigenic drift, not a shift like the one in 2009 that terrified many parents," he said.He said significant body ache accompanied by high fever was another prominent feature of the current influenza strain, ANI reported."A major feature is significant body ache and high fever (103-104°F); this is a key differentiator when comparing COVID-19 or other viruses with the current influenza strain (predominantly H1N1)," he added.Dr Inder Mohan Chugh, vice chairman and HOD, Pulmonology, Yatharth Super Speciality Hospital, Model Town, New Delhi, said children, senior citizens, pregnant women and people with weakened immunity were at higher risk of complications.He said people with conditions including diabetes, heart, kidney or liver disease, cancer, asthma, COPD and other respiratory illnesses were also more vulnerable to complications such as pneumonia."Most influenza cases recover within 7-10 days, but high-risk individuals should seek medical attention promptly."On the use of antibiotics, Chugh said influenza is caused by a virus and should be treated with antivirals rather than antibiotics."Antibiotics do not treat viral influenza; appropriate antiviral treatment may be advised by a doctor, especially when started early. Annual influenza vaccination, hand hygiene, avoiding crowded places when symptomatic, wearing a mask when necessary and maintaining a healthy lifestyle can help reduce the risk of infection and its spread."(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Doctors urge people to take precautions, stay away from crowded places when symptomatic. Those with comorbidities, such as diabetes, hypertension, chronic lung disease, asthma, or neurological issues, are at the highest risk. The current virus is causing more distress among children under five, while high fever was particularly troubling those below two years.
